title: Icon systems and curation
summary: Operational rules for icon meaning, one visual family, reusing the project set, accessible names, decorative hiding, and license metadata. Each rule links the page for that subject.

rules.title: Semantic selection
rules.intent: Choose an icon for the action it starts, and name that action rather than the picture
principles: A functional icon starts an action. Its text alternative states the action, such as Print this page, not a description of the glyph
Name the control for its purpose. A control that closes a dialog is Close, not X
Prefer a symbol people already attach to that task. Novelty is not a reason to pick a glyph
antiPatterns: Same generic sparkles icon for unrelated AI actions
acceptance: The accessible name states the action, and a sighted reviewer can connect the glyph to that action
limitations: WAI and the APG define the name and the function. They do not publish a mandatory icon-to-action dictionary

rules.title: Single visual grammar
rules.intent: Stay inside one icon set, which shares a license, a grid, padding, and either monotone or a fixed palette
principles: An icon set is one design: the same grid and padding, and either monotone or a hardcoded palette, not both
Icons in a toolbar come from that one set so stroke, fill, and corner logic match
Map the chosen set onto the project's icon tokens
antiPatterns: Mixing outline and filled sets in same toolbar
acceptance: The toolbar uses one set, and that set's grid and palette type are named
limitations: Iconify describes how a set is structured. It does not choose the set for a product that already has one

rules.title: Project icon library first
rules.intent: Use the approved set before adding another, because a second set brings a second grid and a second license
principles: Search the project's existing set before opening another collection
Add a new set only when the approved set has no glyph for the action, and record why
Do not take a dependency for one icon that repeats a glyph the project already has
antiPatterns: New dependency for one redundant glyph
acceptance: The project library was checked, and any added set is named with its grid and license
limitations: Iconify defines what a set contains. The requirement to prefer the project's own set is operational guidance for a product that already chose one

rules.title: Icon button accessible name
rules.intent: Give an icon-only button a non-empty accessible name that states the action
principles: A button needs a non-empty accessible name. Text inside the button is the default name
When the button shows only an icon, provide the name with aria-label or aria-labelledby. aria-label hides descendant content from assistive tech, so the name must be the full action
The name matches the visible result: Close, Search, or Print this page
acceptance: The button's accessible name is non-empty and states the action
limitations: ACT rule 97a4e1 checks that a button's name is non-empty. It does not judge whether the wording is the right action. That check is the functional-images tutorial

rules.title: Decorative icon hidden
rules.intent: Hide an icon that adds no information, so assistive tech does not announce the glyph or the file name
principles: If the icon adds nothing beyond adjacent text, give an img an empty alt with no space between the quotes. Omitting alt makes some readers announce the file name
A decorative icon inside a control that already has a name is hidden with aria-hidden, so the glyph is not part of the name
Do not hide an icon that is the only source of the action's name
antiPatterns: Decorative emoji read aloud as action
acceptance: Screen reader output skips the decorative glyph and still announces the control's action
limitations: Whether an icon is decorative is an author judgment, as the WAI tutorial states. An empty alt is for an img. An inline SVG or icon font uses the hiding method that matches how it is embedded

rules.title: Icon license provenance
rules.intent: Record the set's author and license before distributing an icon, because the license applies to the whole set
principles: License is a property of the icon set, not of a single glyph. Record the set name, author, license title, SPDX identifier, and license URL from the set info
Read the license before shipping. An open license can still require attribution or restrict commercial use
Do not embed an SVG whose set and license are unknown
acceptance: Each distributed icon traces to a set, an author, and a license
limitations: Iconify stores the metadata. The legal terms are the license the set names, not Iconify's own summary
